concepts.def: Angles on a line, around a point, in triangles and parallel lines.
Interior and exterior angles of polygons.
Angle and chord properties of circles.
Identical shapes versus same shape, different size.
Accurate drawings using compasses and a ruler.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Geometry — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Geometry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Geometry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11) is:
Which line is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1?
What is the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference subtended by the same arc?
options: The angles are equal because they are subtended by the same arc.
The angle at the centre is half the angle at the circumference.
It means the vectors are parallel.
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: It means the vectors are parallel.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means the vectors are parallel.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Distance between points”?
options: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Positive m: upward slope; negative m: downward; m = 0: horizontal.
If two lines have gradients m₁ and m₂, they are perpendicular ⟺ m₁m₂ = −1.
Radius at point of tangency is perpendicular to tangent. Useful for finding tangent equation.
d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. Pythagoras applied to the coordinate plane.

options: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁). Positive m: upward slope; negative m: downward; m = 0: horizontal.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Equation of a line”?
options: If two lines have gradients m₁ and m₂, they are perpendicular ⟺ m₁m₂ = −1.
d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. Pythagoras applied to the coordinate plane.
(x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² gives circle with centre (a, b) and radius r.
y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) or y = mx + c. Useful forms for different given data.

sequence.def: Steepness m=(y2-y1)/(x2-x1) — the basic building block.
y=mx+c, built directly from a gradient and a point.
Gradients multiply to -1 — uses the gradient idea.
Length √((Δx)²+(Δy)²) via Pythagoras between two points.
Line touching circle at one point, perpendicular to the radius — combines all above.
